title: Backend controllers and edge-relay routes with no named merge target
why: Four server-side surfaces — two NestJS controllers and two edge-relay routes, none of them primary-nav — that the disposition sweep classed MERGE without naming the surface each folds into: all four successor cells read `MERGE_TARGET - the surface it folds into, to be named` with source `REQUIRES SIGNATURE`. The capability names are mostly already present: `S-331`, `S-332` and `S-624` carry owners sourced `EVIDENCE - inventory capabilities`; only `S-629` (`set_visit_mood`) has no capability named on its row, which is why it is the single row needing both signatures. What the owner is signing here is therefore the merge target, not a name for what each route does. These are not UI decisions — authority stays server-side, and none of the four is among the 101 primary-nav entries collapsing to 5.
disappear: Not nothing. Every one of the four rows carries `RETIRE AFTER PARITY - K16`, so each route is scheduled to retire once its merge target proves parity — later, not in this package. The two clearest are the `/api/client-link/consume` relay, which has zero callers in all three bundles while the live challenge flow goes direct to NestJS, and which must retire together with the backend route at `webhook_server.py:10012`; and the stray `set_visit_mood` dispatch case, which moves to sit with the other six consent/relay cases. The one thing that must not disappear into a merge is the consent half of `/api/customers`.
remain: All eight paths across the four rows stay reachable until parity is proven at K16: five on `/api/customers` (GET and PATCH `me/profile`, GET `/`, GET `/:userId`, PATCH `/:userId/notes`), `GET /api/crm/providers`, the client-link consume relay, and the `set_visit_mood` dispatch case. Their existing role decorators remain exactly as written — `me/profile` carries no `@Roles` and belongs to the data subject (any authenticated tenant member), the two registry reads and the notes write are `CUSTOMER_MANAGER_ROLES`, and `/api/crm/providers` stays `@Public()`. The action string `set_visit_mood` must survive the move verbatim: it is the contract with `app.html:13543` and the relay route table. `/api/crm/providers` must keep advertising planned providers as planned.
risk: MEDIUM-HIGH — this is not naming only; all four rows carry a hazard that a careless merge realises. `/api/customers` is the worst: `me/profile` is 152-ФЗ machinery belonging to the data subject, and folding it into the manager-gated registry would put a person's own consent record behind someone else's role; the controller is additionally gated `@RequiresFeature('customers.core')` at L44, so a merged surface inheriting a different feature gate would silently strip consent management from any tenant without that entitlement. `/api/client-link/consume` is an orphan with zero callers, and naive removal leaves the backend route at `webhook_server.py:10012` reachable with no client — an unexercised, untested authority path left open. Smaller but real: flattening `/api/crm/providers`' planned providers into available ones would have onboarding offer a CRM connection that does not exist, discovered only after credentials are entered; and a changed `set_visit_mood` action string breaks mood writes silently — the relay answers 400 `invalid_client_command` and the PWA shows no error, as it shows none for any failed mood write today.
user_impact: Signing G15 changes nothing a user can see — it fixes four rows' successor/owner columns and deploys no bytes. All four surfaces are server-side: two NestJS controllers (S-331 /api/customers, S-332 /api/crm/providers) and two PHP relay dispatch cases (S-624 client_link_consume, S-629 set_visit_mood). What keeps working after the downstream MERGE, verified: an owner still gets the CRM catalogue at the onboarding CRM stage (app.html:17557-17562, maya-os-site/index.html:15359-15364 both fetch /crm/providers); a manager/owner still sees the same client registry in the business cabinet (app.html:12456, 12488, 34239 → GET /customers). Two corrections to the shipped-surface picture. (1) No shipped bundle calls /api/customers/me/profile — the current PWA writes consent to /client-channel/consent, and scripts/maya-identity/verify-native.cjs:14 asserts the consent block does NOT contain '/customers/me/profile'; the controller's own comment (customers.controller.ts:66-68) names its only live callers: native builds installed before e5ec27fd. So the consent half of S-331 is legacy-compat for already-installed apps, not a surface today's PWA exercises. (2) set_visit_mood has three live call sites, not one: app.html:13543 and maya-os-site/index.html:11709 (both via mayaClientPreferenceCall, which rejects on !r.ok || value.error) and app-tenant.html:7413 (a bare fetch with an unconditional `.catch(() => {})`). The only user-visible outcomes this group can produce are failure modes, and the two are not equal. The mood write already fails silently today: `window.__toast` is read at four guarded call sites and assigned nowhere in the repo, so every mood-write failure — network, 403, or a drifted action string producing 400 invalid_client_command — is invisible; the move adds one more way to enter an already-silent path rather than creating the silence. The CRM one is not silent: the server independently refuses a non-connectable provider at connect time (crm.service.ts:4578-4595, 400 crm_provider_not_available) and the PWA already recovers from that 400, so a mis-merged "planned as available" catalogue is a visible, recoverable dead-end after credentials are entered. One structural note on S-629: the only api-proxy.php in the repository is the sanitized test fixture (maya-saas-backend/test/fixtures/beget/api-proxy.sanitized.php); the authoritative file is the deployed Beget copy, so the relocation must be made there and re-mirrored — fixture/prod drift is itself a failure mode alongside action-string drift.
security_impact: Naming itself changes nothing: all four surfaces are server-side and no authority check is removed by attaching a capability name. No client-side *authority* check is involved (S-332 does feed a client-side fail-closed provider filter, but crm.service.ts:4578-4595 re-checks connectable/productionReady server-side regardless). The MERGE work these rows schedule carries one conditional improvement and three live risks. Improvement, correctly conditioned: converging S-624 closes a second, internet-reachable front door to the same client-identity authority transition — Beget api-proxy.php case client_link_consume (fixture L2128) → webhook_server.py:10012 → legacy_client_command_bridge → NestJS /api/internal/legacy/client-commands/consume — with zero callers in all three PWA bundles while the live flow runs on the SaaS API path (/client-channel/challenges then /client-channel/consume, app.html:25244-25261), not through api-proxy.php; but only if the relay case and the backend handler retire together, since removing only the relay leaves an untested authority path reachable. Risk 1, S-331: GET/PATCH /api/customers/me/profile (L52, L58) carry no @Roles and are the data subject's own 152-ФЗ record, while GET / (L92), GET /:userId (L105) and PATCH /:userId/notes (L115) are @Roles(...CUSTOMER_MANAGER_ROLES); folding the consent half into the manager-gated registry would put a person's own consent record behind someone else's role, and the controller-wide @RequiresFeature('customers.core') at L44 means a merged surface inheriting a different feature gate would silently strip consent management from a tenant lacking that entitlement. This is worse than a misplaced read: PATCH me/profile is a consent *write* that routes the legacy consent-only shape through submitLegacyNativeConsent into the canonical client-channel consent boundary (L66-88), and its only live callers are pre-e5ec27fd installed native builds — a break here cannot be repaired by shipping a new frontend. Risk 2, S-629: the relay case carries no authority check of its own (the key allow-list, the bot's channel_proof and the handler's record-ownership check do), so relocating it cannot remove one — but the visit-mood path is split across two groups and two packages: S-629 sits in G15 (K5/K8, MERGE) while set_visit_mood_handler, the half that enforces record ownership, is S-634 in O08 (K15, SECURITY/AUTHORITY ONLY). The "move/retire together" condition stated for S-624 therefore applies to S-629 as well, across a package boundary that lets the editable half desynchronise from the frozen one. Risk 3, S-332: both /crm/providers and /features/registry are @Public() with no tenant context, so the merge as proposed is authority-neutral — but the target is unnamed, and this is the only G15 row touching a public surface. A merged readiness surface that answered from per-tenant entitlements (GET /features/effective on the same controller is authenticated and @TenantScoped) would convert a public catalogue into a tenant-state leak; one that gained a gate instead would fail the pre-auth onboarding CRM stage closed. Neither claim touches a frozen limitation: nothing here asserts STEP_UP reachability, Gate 10 enforcement, separation of duties, or client-confirmed attendance.
